plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole avenues turn into clouds of violet-blue as thousands of trumpet-shaped blossoms open on bare-looking branches and then carpet the pavement below. The trees are so closely tied to the city that Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere, peaking in October (roughly late September to November)
plants.location: Pretoria, South Africa, where the trees line the streets, and in other warm temperate cities of the Southern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: The jacaranda is native to South America, not Africa. It was introduced to Pretoria in the 1800s, and the city now has tens of thousands of them.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: Dense, many-petalled blooms in gold, white, crimson and bronze fill temple gardens, parks and festival displays as the autumn air cools. Growers time late-blooming varieties to peak in mid-October.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn, from September through November, with peak displays in mid-October
plants.location: Japan, in gardens, parks and chrysanthemum festivals throughout the country
plants.funFact: The chrysanthemum is Japan's imperial flower. The Chrysanthemum Throne is the traditional name for the seat of the emperor.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: When most borders are fading, this bulb sends up bare stems topped with sparkling umbels of wavy, ribbon-petalled pink flowers. The petals shimmer in low autumn light, and the straplike leaves appear only after flowering.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn, with September and October the best months for flowering
plants.location: Gardens in Britain and other temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere (native to South Africa)
plants.funFact: Bowden lilies are summer-dormant. They flower on leafless stems and put up their leaves only once the weather cools in autumn, which is the reverse of most garden bulbs.
